QF.id: AIFM CIII Legal Documents and Negotiations_3

question.text: Satpura Market-Neutral Fund (a Cat III trust-form AIF) is about to launch its third scheme under the same trust. From a legal-documentation standpoint, which of the following BEST describes the Investment Management Agreement (IMA)?

answer.text: A fresh IMA must be signed at the launch of every scheme because each scheme has a different NAV series.
The IMA is entered into between each investor and the Investment Manager, scheme by scheme.
The IMA is signed ONCE for the trust as a whole (between the Trustee on behalf of the AIF and the Investment Manager) and is not re-signed at each scheme launch.
The IMA is signed between SEBI and the Investment Manager as part of the registration process.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9.3 states: 'The IMA is signed once for the trust as a whole and not signed at the launch of each scheme.' It is between the Trustee (on behalf of the AIF) and the Investment Manager, and the Trustee delegates all management powers (except retained powers specified in the Trust Indenture). The Trap: Option A confuses scheme-level PPM filings with trust-level IMA. Option B confuses the IMA with the Contribution/Subscription Agreement. Option D incorrectly casts SEBI as a contracting party — SEBI is a regulator, not a counterparty. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C All-Cat Manager covers the same once-per-trust rule. XIX-B Cat III Distributor may frame this as a 'disclosure' question. XXI-B Portfolio Managers sign a PM-agreement per client, which is a different model. Manager's Pro-Tip: On a multi-scheme Cat III trust, review the IMA's 'retained powers' clause carefully — typically valuation-committee constitution and manager removal sit with the Trustee, while day-to-day long-short sizing sits with the Manager.
